title: Explain why an AGV can move out without a replacement (exchange/backfill gap) during AGV exchange pairing
summary: Use the OptiSweep exchange pairing rule to explain an observed “AGV moves out without another one to replace it.” The source-backed mechanism is that OptiSweep sends the exchange commands as a paired action; therefore, a visible gap typically indicates the trailing AGV behind the departing AGV had a fault / was not backfilled properly. The source also describes a timing edge case where the trailing AGV is reported ready for a new task and completes/faults at the same time, which can lead to improper backfill.
when_to_use: When you need to interpret the source-backed reason an AGV appears to depart during an exchange pairing without a replacement AGV backfilling it.
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Provide the source-backed explanation for the exchange/backfill gap mechanism (paired commands + trailing AGV fault/backfill issue) and determine whether the observed behavior matches the described edge case.
Escalation (if needed): If the observed behavior cannot be explained by the source-backed mechanism, escalate for deeper system evidence beyond this training segment.
access_or_tools_needed: Training video segment transcript (00:28:37.000 to 00:32:10.000) for the pairing/backfill explanation

visual_references.description: Source frame containing the pairing/backfill explanation: front AGV will not move until the AGV behind it is available; software sends both commands at the same time; gap can occur when the trailing AGV faults / is not backfilled properly; timing edge case where trailing AGV is ready for a new task and completes/faults at the same time; chute closure tied to chute being full.

steps.title: Apply the exchange pairing rule (front AGV movement depends on the trailing AGV)
steps.purpose: Establish the source-backed constraint that explains why a replacement AGV should normally be present when the front AGV moves.
steps.instruction: Use the source pairing rule: the front AGV will not move until the AGV behind it is available for the paired exchange command, because OptiSweep sends both exchange commands at the same time.
steps.expected_result: Your interpretation is consistent with the rule that the exchange command to leave is only sent when there is an AGV behind it (paired commands).
steps.healthy_condition: The observed behavior you are explaining aligns with a paired exchange mechanism (front movement implies a trailing AGV was available for the paired command).
steps.failure_condition: You observe an exchange/backfill gap (front AGV moves out without a replacement) that appears inconsistent with the paired-command rule.

actions.label: Recall pairing rule
actions.exact_action: Recall the pairing rule from the source: the front AGV will not move until the AGV behind it is available for the paired exchange command; literally our software sends both commands at the same time.

source_evidence.quote: “the only time it can happen is if the AGV behind it has a fault because the front AGV will not move until AGV behind it. Literally our software sends both commands at the same time. So they get sent together.”

steps.healthy_condition: The trailing AGV is consistent with being faulted / not backfilled properly at the time the front AGV departed (matching the source’s described only-time condition).
steps.failure_condition: The observed behavior cannot be explained by the trailing AGV fault/backfill mechanism described by the source.

actions.label: Assess trailing AGV fault/backfill
actions.exact_action: Check whether the AGV behind it has a fault (the only time it can happen) and whether it was not backfilled properly.

steps.purpose: Provide source-backed context that chute closure is tied to chute fullness, not merely both AGVs being in the station, which can help interpret downstream effects.
